note: PRC-18. Nothing in this project exercised gamepad input before this file -- Joypad/JoyButton/JoyMotion returned zero hits across every .gd and every tools/*.py. This scenario drives dialog-skip, cursor and build+select through genuinely device-shaped InputEventJoypadMotion/InputEventJoypadButton events (the `gamepad` verb), not the action-shaped InputEventAction `press` already used elsewhere, proving LF-139's Input.parse_input_event() mechanism generalises to real controller input. First finding from building this: lf_build and lf_confirm share the SAME device-0 button-0 binding in project.godot, and dialog_view.gd's _unhandled_input() deliberately consumes lf_confirm with set_input_as_handled() while the anchor-01 boot brief (4 lines) is still showing -- 'so the gamepad button that advances a line does not also place an emplacement' (that file's own comment). A real player hits this too: the first button-0 presses page through the brief; only once it is fully dismissed does the same button reach the board. Every gamepad action's effect is observable the FOLLOWING frame (same one-frame queueing delay as press/cursor). PLC-06 UPDATE: the exact-slot assertions this scenario used to make (`sim.placed.0.slot_x/y == 2,3`, `view.selected_slot.x/y == 2,3`) exploited a fixed-slot-graph behaviour that no longer exists -- `_step_cursor()`'s first press used to park the cursor on `slots[0]` regardless of direction; free placement has no slot graph to park on, so the single axis nudge below now moves the continuous cursor a sub-tile step from the board's own centre, lands short of anchor-01's vertical lane segment (still inside its standoff), and `lf_build`'s snap-to-legal search (PLC-06's `_find_build_pos()`) is what actually finds the nearest legal spot and builds there -- a MORE interesting thing for this scenario to prove than the old coincidental slot number, and proof that the snap mechanism itself works from a genuinely device-shaped input, not just from `press`. The exact landing position is deterministic (no RNG anywhere in this path) but is no longer the point of the assertion, so it is only sanity-bounded (on the board, past the lane standoff) rather than pinned to a magic float that would need re-deriving by hand every time the snap search's own tie-breaking changed.
